snippets.output: Muscle strain is a common injury that can be caused by overuse, overstretching, or direct blows to the muscle.
The duration of pain from muscle strain can vary depending on the severity of the injury and the individual's overall health.
Mild muscle strains typically resolve on their own within 7-14 days.
More severe muscle strains may take longer to heal, often requiring 4-6 weeks or more for full recovery.

Factors that can influence the healing time include the location of the strain, the severity of the injury, and the effectiveness of treatment. Strains in the lower back may take longer to heal than those in the upper body.

If pain from a muscle strain persists or worsens over time, it may be a sign of a more serious underlying condition, such as a herniated disc or a stress fracture. Medical attention should be sought in such cases.
